turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey Joanna, quick question — I saw you removed the e2e suite from the pipeline yesterday. What's the deal?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Oh, yeah. They were taking like 20 minutes per run and blocking every merge. I figured we could ship faster without them, you know? Just for now.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hmm, I get the speed thing, but those tests catch real regressions. You sure you want to go without them?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Honestly, we've been fine for weeks. I'll add them back if anything breaks. Promise.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So... the app broke right after release. Like, 20 minutes ago. Check the error logs.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The checkout flow — looks like a race condition we never caught. And guess what? The e2e tests would've caught it. The ones you deleted.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Ugh. You're right. I'm putting them back in the pipeline right now. And I'll write a new test for this exact scenario.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good call. Better late than never, I guess.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, just saw the release went out clean this morning. App's been healthy all day — nice work on bringing the tests back.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Thanks. Yeah, I kept the e2e tests in the pipeline this time, no shortcuts. Feels way more solid.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Also, I noticed you ran the database migration during peak traffic yesterday. That was... bold.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I thought it'd be fine — the migration was supposed to be non-blocking. But it locked the database for like 15 minutes. Orders were stuck.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: A few support tickets, but we rolled back fast. Lesson learned — never again during peak hours. I'll schedule it for 2 AM next time.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yeah, that's probably wise. At least the app's healthy now, so we're back on track.
